entityDescription:
IS-Wireless develops and delivers 5G networking solutions. These include standard-compliant software and hardware necessary to build 5G (and also 4G) telco networks by MNO, MVNOs, private institutions, municipalities and many more.
5G is understood here not only as one of the 3GPP releases (5G NR) but, primarily, as a new paradigm needed for the coming networking revolution, where better performance is delivered at a lower cost. This cannot be done by just copying the network architectures and business models from previous generations (2G, 3G, 4G). The new approach is necessary, where network functionality is fully software-defined (i.e., virtualized) and can be run on any COST hardware. What follows, such new network infrastructure can be offered in models known to software industry, such as SaaS (or rather Infrastructure-as-a-Service).
IS-Wireless specializes in software solutions for the Radio Access Network (RAN) part, which is the most costly, cross-disciplinary and challenging part of telecom network. 1000x higher capacity can only be provided with a much denser RAN network, where spectrum is reused aggressively by numerous low-power low-cost Radio Heads. Interference problems need to be solved, QoS needs to be provided and all these should happen at a lower network CAPEX and OPEX. This makes RAN the critical part of 5G.
IS-Wireless is strongly rooted in R&D on 4G and 5G. In 2006 the company started operation and provided a complete design of special-purpose broadband access system for one of the providers of Polish MOD. In 2009 the company started experimenting with 4G software implementations focusing on PHY and MAC layers. In 2012 IS-Wireless started participation in EU-funded collaborative projects on 5G, with partners such as Alcatel-Lucent, Intel, Atos, Fraunhofer Institute and many more. In 2018 IS-Wireless received Round-A funding for work on software-defined 5G networking (including RAN, core and MANO).

IS-Wireless specializes in software solutions for the Radio Access Network (RAN) part, which is the most costly, cross-disciplinary and challenging part of telecom network. 1000x higher capacity can only be provided with a much denser RAN network, where spectrum is reused aggressively by numerous low-power low-cost Radio Heads. Interference problems need to be solved, QoS needs to be provided and all these should happen at a lower network CAPEX and OPEX. This makes RAN the critical part of 5G.
IS-Wireless is strongly rooted in R&D on 4G and 5G. In 2006 the company started operation and provided a complete design of special-purpose broadband access system for one of the providers of Polish MOD. In 2009 the company started experimenting with 4G software implementations focusing on PHY and MAC layers. In 2012 IS-Wireless started participation in EU-funded collaborative projects on 5G, with partners such as Alcatel-Lucent, Intel, Atos, Fraunhofer Institute and many more. In 2018 IS-Wireless received Round-A funding for work on software-defined 5G networking (including RAN, core and MANO).

Ayuda en Acción (AeA) is an independent, non-political and non-confessional Spanish development cooperation organization aimed to promote structural changes to contribute to the eradication of poverty. It works to improve the living conditions of the most disadvantaged communities through self-sustaining development programmes.
AeA has 38 years of experience in proposal design, planning, managing and implementing development projects. Currently, our work is supported by more than 105,000 collaborators and 645 companies and public institutions, as well as volunteer personnel, who contribute to the work that the organization implements in 18 countries in Latin America, Asia, Africa and also in Spain and Portugal. We promote more than 120 cooperation and integral development programmes that improve the living conditions of more than 2 million people who suffer, or are at risk of suffering, poverty, inequality and social exclusion. In compliance with its internal policies, it promotes equal opportunities for men and women in its labour structure; thus, at the close of this financial year, 55% of the workforce and 40% of decision-making positions are held by women.
Ayuda en Acción recognizes rights holders in all persons and works with others so that they can exercise their rights fully and on their own. swyMed is the only Live Video Medicine platform built specifically for healthcare providers who want to provide high-quality care to their patients even in the most challenging network conditions.

Live Video Medicine (LVM) is telemedicine provided through a real-time audio and video connection between one or more medical professionals and a patient. Over the last five years, the use of LVM has been slowly introduced in pre-hospital care, ambulatory or clinic care, and home settings for conditions that require, among other things, a rapid visual assessment (Critical Care and Emergency Medicine) or a strong patient-doctor relationship (mental illnesses or chronic conditions—diabetes, heart failure, COPD). Over 230 million patients in the USA alone suffer from diseases that can be treated through LVM and the cost for treating such diseases is expected to more than double over the next 15 years from $700 billion today to almost $1.5 trillion by 2030 if left unchecked. Live video medicine will fundamentally change the way health care providers work. swyMed is the most effective Live Video Medicine solution available on the market today.

Fundación Cibervoluntarios is a non-profit organization shaped by social entrepreneurs that promote the use and knowledge of new technologies as a means to alleviate social gaps, generate social innovation and foster citizen empowerment. 
We were born in December 2001 and, after 3 years as an Association, in 2005 we became a Foundation under the protectorate of the Ministry of Culture of the Spanish Government. We have been working for 19 years with a main goal: to empower people through the social use of ICTs, thanks to a growing network of social and technological volunteers: the cybervolunteers, community leaders that seek, detect and analyse social needs within their local environment and improve it through actions, activities and free training in several digital skills, tools and applications for collectives at risk of social/digital exclusion, fostering at the same time citizen empowerment.
Our main strenght is promote citizen participation, in this way we have developed an innovative platform Empodera.org supported by the United Nations to foster Citizen Participation for SDGs.
Our long path is based on collaboration with other entities and organizations. From our Foundation, we can contribute with our network of 1.500 cybervolunteers who perform direct actions to a network of more than 700 grass roots organisations of different collectives throughout Spain (NGOS, Associations, educational centres, municipalities….). The cybervolunteers generate their own projects, framed by social innovation, from local to global, through the use of new tools to solve old problems in a different way. Cibervoluntarios is pioneer in technological volunteering in Spain.
We help groups of people that may be excluded from information society for their gender, age, professional and/or social environment, lack of time, knowledge, skills, motivation and/or material or economic resources... Our cybervolunteers manage to adapt the use of technological applications to alleviate these social gaps at all levels: work environment, participation, health,. …
All this work has received several recognitions: to“the creation of new forms of participation and social innovation in support of groups at risk of exclusion”, received from the hands of the former Prince and Princess of Asturias in 2011, the economic and social recognition of Google.org, for being one of 50 entities that are changing the world, and the social recognition of the Financial Times as one of “Europe’s 100 digital champions” in 2018. WSIS Prize 2016, In the category “Ethical dimensions of the Information Society”

Foundation goals are:
1. To encourage the adoption and use of ICT by citizens, NGOs and institutions.
2. To promote a responsible and appropriate use of the contents, services, tools and access to Information Society and Knowledge.
3. To promote the creation, training and mobilization of a technological volunteer: the cybervolunteers.
4. To create a social conscience: to generate positive social and cultural attitudes towards the importance of New Technologies for the development and advancement of society.
5. To remove any barriers that prevent knowledge and use of new technologies, especially the physical, social and cultural ones.
6. To encourage participation through ICT and the responsible use of these tools among the youth.
